claim: The tracer particles are excited at 620 nm, as specified by the supplier for the product family.
validity_conditions: As with the emission peak, a band reported as a point: no width is printed, so none is asserted. Diameter-independent. WHETHER THIS LINE CAN ACTUALLY BE DELIVERED IS A SEPARATE QUESTION and is not answered here -- which light engine reaches the sample, and at what wavelength, lives in kb/staging/devices.v0.json under light_engines, and the lapp_branch_assignment gap there is still open. A tracer that is excitable at 620 nm and an instrument that can excite it are two facts, and only the first is on this data sheet. 015 WAS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY IT WAS ISSUED, AND THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT THE TYPE. For a few hours this entry read that the product identification had been withdrawn and that it was not about the bottle on this bench. The person reversed that on 2026-09-19 after the prior project's records were opened: the bottle IS AFR-0500-COOH, and what is wrong is Abvigen's published data. WHAT DECIDED IT WAS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and that is worth keeping because the measurement alone did not settle it. Both explanations -- wrong bottle, or wrong data sheet -- predict green-excited particles visible at 605, and 015's own evidence, a label that says nothing, is equally consistent with either. What broke the tie is that the Abvigen page has two documented errors unrelated to any of this (a monoclonal-antibody filing, and the product name printed in the Particle Size field), so `the data sheet is wrong` is far the cheaper explanation. See abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable. AND THE ENTRY IS STILL NOT DIRECTLY ABOUT THE BOTTLE. Under the instance/type split architecture ruled in 6eaee1b, this is a fact about the TYPE `AFR-0500-COOH`, at E3, from the supplier. The bottle is an INSTANCE and lives in the sample table. The claim joining them -- `this bottle is that product` -- carries its own grade and is E5, because the label is still silent and the person's judgement is what stands in for it; it becomes E3 the day somebody reads a label that says. So applying anything here to the particles on the bench inherits E5 by 5.8, worst in the chain. Restored, but not restored to E3. THE `abvigen_` HANDLES STAY, and they are now right for a different reason than the one they were changed for. They were renamed from `tracer_` because the word `tracer` asserted these were ours in a string nothing checks; they keep the name because these are type-level facts and the type is what they should be named for. A query for our tracer should not land here. THIS NUMBER IS DISPROVED. Not one side of a live conflict and not merely doubted: two independent observations on two different instruments in two different projects agree against it. This bench, 2026-09-19 (particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, E2): the particles fluoresce under green excitation and show through a 605 band. The prior project, 2026-09-05 and -09-06: the same catalogue product tested CYAN ~2000 ADU, GREEN ~3500 ADU, RED none at all -- the exact reverse of what a 620 nm excitation predicts -- and then measured through four bandpasses, strongest at 589-610 nm against 677-701 nm at 17.2 percent, with two anti-Stokes controls holding the floor at 0.4 percent. That project set both of this product's published spectral figures to null and renamed its dye registry entry from AbvigenRed680 to AbvigenRed. Kept under rule 8, not deleted, because the next person to read this data sheet will propose this number again and needs to meet the record that it was tested and failed. A published specification being wrong about the thing it describes is itself worth knowing. The prior project's numbers are NOT entered here: they are E3 about THEIR bottle and applying them to ours would add a same-stock E5 assumption on top, when our own E2 says the same thing about our own bench. What crossed is the finding about the vendor's published data, which is about Abvigen and attaches to no bottle at all.

identifiers.applies_to: the type AFR-0500-COOH. Applying it to the bottle on this bench goes through the E5 linking claim in the sample table
